speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help me pinpoint the cause, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it radiates down a specific arm or finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Myelopathy (likely due to degenerative cervical spondylosis).

I have noted your age, the one-year history of burning pain and paresthesias, the progression of bilateral hand weakness over three months, and your vascular risk factors. Given the neurological decline, I need to see your cervical spine MRI immediately to evaluate for spinal cord compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI
